name: 'Ori Tahiti (Foundation)
notes: 'Ori Tahiti foundation pack (Doc 04 template; foundation-forward, the Oceania wave's only pack — ON PURPOSE). The oceanian family holds four forms and three are community-held: hula (kahiko and the hālau tradition), haka (ancestral iwi practice), and poi — this app builds NO packs for them; docs/OCEANIA-PARTNERSHIPS.md holds the plan for their people to author them if they choose. 'Ori Tahiti qualifies for a foundation because its own history says so: suppressed under missionary-era codes from the 1820s, rebuilt in public through the 20th century — Madeleine Moua's troupe Heiva (1956) is the credited revival landmark — and today carried by the Heiva i Tahiti festival and a worldwide school scene LED BY TAHITIAN TEACHERS, including online schools taught from Tahiti itself. Design truths: the tō'ere (slit log drum) commands the 'ōte'a — its pehe patterns are in this app's Rhythm Trainer; the posture (bent knees, level still upper body) is the non-negotiable base; hip vocabulary is heavily gated (tāmau sway → 'ami circles → fa'arapu's fast circles, the signature that earns its own endurance gate); meta.fenua_honesty gates all movement — the fenua's teachers hold this dance, and the pack's job is to deliver you to them prepared and respectful.

seasons.finale: Film yourself clapping the tō'ere pattern through one full 'ōte'a track — the drum's command, heard.
Film the base: knees bent, back tall, upper body level and still while the knees pulse — the foundation everything rides on.
Film slow 'ami circles both directions over the posture — hips alone, shoulders like a shelf.
Film 20 honest seconds of fa'arapu — small, fast, from the knees, upper body untouched. Build seconds, not blur.
Watch a full Heiva i Tahiti performance — then enroll with a Tahitian-led school, online or local. The fenua's teachers take it from here.

attributes.name: Bent-knee endurance L1
attributes.test: 2 minutes standing in the bent-knee base, back tall, without the knees straightening or the back bowing

attributes.name: Hip isolation L1
attributes.test: 20 slow hip circles each direction with the ribcage pinned — a book balanced on your head shouldn't wobble

attributes.name: Drum-dance stamina L2
attributes.test: one full 'ōte'a track of continuous knee-pulse and hipwork without the posture collapsing

nodes.name: The tō'ere commands the 'ōte'a
checkpoints: the tō'ere — the slit log drum struck with a stick — drives the 'ōte'a with fast wooden pehe patterns; one is in this app's Rhythm Trainer
the pahu's deep skin-drum pulse anchors underneath; hips answer the tō'ere, feet answer the pahu
the drummers change pehe and the dancers change step — like capoeira's berimbau and bomba's primo, the conversation rules the floor

nodes.name: 'Ōte'a and 'aparima — drum dance and song dance
checkpoints: 'ōte'a: the percussion dance — drums only, fast hips, the form the world knows
'aparima: the song dance — ukulele and voice, the HANDS narrate the lyrics' story, gentle and seated or standing
hear the difference in ten seconds; the two forms are one culture's two temperatures

nodes.name: Banned and rebuilt — the revival credited
checkpoints: 'ori Tahiti was SUPPRESSED under missionary-era codes from the 1820s — public dance banned for over a century as colonial and church authorities outlawed it

the 20th-century rebuild is credited: Madeleine Moua founded the troupe Heiva in 1956 and put Tahitian dance back on public stages with pride; the modern Heiva i Tahiti festival carries the flame every July
another dance the bans could not kill — this app's shelves keep filling with them, and each one is a lesson

nodes.name: The fenua's schools — Tahitian teachers worldwide
checkpoints: 'ori Tahiti is carried by schools in Tahiti and a worldwide scene of studios and online academies LED BY TAHITIAN TEACHERS — unusually accessible for a Pacific tradition, on the fenua's own terms
solo competitions and the Heiva's group categories set the art's standards; watch full Heiva performances to see the ceiling
its Pacific siblings — hula, haka, poi — are community-held in this app: no packs, by design; their peoples' doors are the only doors (see the partnership brief)

nodes.name: The honest limit: the fenua's teachers hold this dance
checkpoints: this pack is preparation, not membership: 'ori Tahiti's technique, costume, chant and meaning are taught by Tahitian teachers and schools — several teach online from Tahiti itself, so the real thing is genuinely reachable
what solo prep honestly owns: the tō'ere ear, the bent-knee posture, gated hip vocabulary, and respect for what each movement means before performing any of it
arrive at a school knowing the drum, the base, and Madeleine Moua's name — prepared and humble is the whole assignment

nodes.name: The base — bent knees, level stillness
checkpoints: knees bent and springy, feet flat and grounded, back tall, shoulders level — the upper body rides like a shelf that never tips
the knee pulse keeps the drum's time; everything the hips will ever do is powered from here
endurance IS the technique: Heiva dancers hold this base through entire drum suites
mistakes: knees straightening the moment attention moves to the hips (the base is a discipline, not a starting pose)
the back bowing forward to fake depth

nodes.name: Tāmau — the side-to-side sway
checkpoints: hips sway side to side driven by alternating knee extension — the knees are the engine, the hips are the result
upper body still as water; the sway lives below the ribs entirely
slow with the pahu, doubled with the tō'ere — the timing trades are the drill
mistakes: swaying from the waist with lazy knees (the engine is BELOW)

nodes.name: 'Ami — the hip circle
checkpoints: the hips draw a full smooth circle — knees trading depth to steer it, upper body untouched
both directions, equally, slow before anything: a perfect slow 'ami is the prerequisite the fa'arapu will audit
the raqs pack's circles and the wine are distant cousins; the Tahitian engine (knee-driven, flat-footed) is its own machine — learn THIS one on its own terms
mistakes: an oval sold as a circle (film from behind; the shape doesn't lie)

nodes.name: Fa'arapu — the fast circles
nodes.anchor: the signature — earned in seconds, kept in years
checkpoints: the 'ami small and FAST — a rapid continuous hip circle from quick alternating knee drive, the upper body a statue above it
build in honest seconds: 5 clean, then 10, then 20 — speed with a wobbling shelf is zero progress
relaxation is the accelerator (the shimmy's law, the samba's law, the same law): tension is what can't spin
varu (the figure-8) branches from here — circles first, always
mistakes: shaking instead of circling (film from behind: a fa'arapu ROTATES)
holding the breath (the statue above still breathes)

nodes.name: 'Aparima hands (intro)
checkpoints: the 'aparima's hands narrate — waves, rain, love, the island itself, gestured over the gentle sway
soft wrists, meaning first: know what a gesture says before you perform it (the fenua's teachers hold the vocabulary; this node is the introduction, not the dictionary)
the buchaechum's breath and the persian pack's framing are kin disciplines — story carried in calm hands

nodes.name: The foundation suite — filmed
checkpoints: one 'ōte'a track: the base held throughout, tāmau riding the pahu, slow 'ami both ways, and your honest seconds of fa'arapu
film from behind for the circles and from the side for the posture — both angles must pass
the shelf test: could a glass of water ride your shoulders? That's the whole foundation in one image

nodes.name: The fenua's school
checkpoints: watch one full Heiva i Tahiti performance — the festival films are the tradition's own showcase
enroll with a Tahitian-led school: online academies teach from Tahiti itself, and Tahitian-taught studios exist across the diaspora
arrive with the drum in your ear, the base in your legs, and the revival's story in your mouth — the fenua's teachers take it from here
